missing_spec_content.spec_text: An example of how the growth of tourism in an LIC or NEE helps to reduce the development gap.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson's example places Kenya in a different category: "In Kenya, a lower-middle-income country, about 2 million tourists came in 2019" (keyPoints[4].content). It never says Kenya is an LIC or an NEE, so a student cannot tell that the example meets the spec requirement. The lesson also gives figures for a single year only (2019). It does not show the growth of tourism over time, which is what the spec asks for.

above_gcse.text: Learn the difference: the range is highest minus lowest; the interquartile range is the upper quartile minus the lower quartile.
above_gcse.why: Neither 3.2.2.1 nor 3.2.2.2 requires this statistical content, and the lesson teaches nothing that links to it. It could confuse a student revising development.

factual_errors.text: A rate is always "per" something: births, deaths or infant deaths for every 1,000 people (or 1,000 births) each year.
factual_errors.correction: Not every development rate is per 1,000 per year. The literacy rate, which the lesson itself lists and defines as "the share of adults who can read and write", is a percentage. Birth, death and infant mortality rates are per 1,000 per year; other rates are not.

factual_errors.text: A rate is per 1,000 people (or births) per year
factual_errors.correction: This holds only for birth, death and infant mortality rates. The literacy rate is a percentage of adults.

factual_errors.text: Under one international scheme, 36 countries have had debts cancelled.
factual_errors.correction: Somalia reached the HIPC completion point in December 2023. That makes 37 of the 39 eligible countries receiving full HIPC relief, not 36. In addition, HIPC relief reduces debt; it does not necessarily cancel all of it.

factual_errors.text: Debt relief: cancelled debt frees money for health and schools; 36 countries helped
factual_errors.correction: 37 of the 39 eligible countries had received full HIPC relief after Somalia reached completion point in December 2023.

factual_errors.text: Aid is money, goods or skills given, not lent or earned.
factual_errors.correction: Aid can include loans. Official development assistance covers concessional (low-interest) loans as well as grants, so aid is not only gifts.

not_checked: Sourced figures dated 2025–2026 could not be verified against the live World Bank, IMF or Grameen Bank sources: GNI per head 2025 (USA $88,810, UK $54,550, Nigeria $1,360, Niger $750), the Grameen Bank figures for August 2026, and extreme poverty of 10% in 2024 at $3.00/day.
